I'll build a single-file HTML game: `index.html`. Top-down train game inspired by Dead Rails, mobile-first, portrait orientation, fixed viewport (100dvh), no scrolling.

Game design:
- Canvas full-screen, portrait.
- Train on tracks running vertically (world scrolls downward as train moves "forward" north). Actually top-down: train moves up; camera follows.
- Train auto-moves; player controls a character (joystick) that can be on the train or off collecting resources (fuel, wood, coal, scrap, food).
- Fuel depletes as train moves; refuel with coal/wood.
- Distance milestone (like reaching 1000m = win, similar to Dead Rails reaching the end).
- Obstacles/zombies? Keep simple: enemies at stations that chase player. Player has simple attack maybe. Keep scope manageable but playable.
- Controls: virtual joystick on left, action buttons on right (interact/collect, board/leave, refuel).
- UI: fuel bar, distance, resources counts, buttons.
- States: on train (player follows train automatically), off train (free movement).

Simplify: The train runs along a straight vertical track at fixed x. Resources scattered along the track in the terrain. Player walks with joystick; when near resource, auto-collect by walking over it (or tap button). When near train and train stopped, board.

Mechanic: "Stop/Go" button toggles train moving. Fuel drains while moving. When fuel out, train stops. Resource nodes: wood, coal, scrap, food. Distance goal e.g. 2000m. Enemies wander near resource clusters; touching hurts player (health). Player can attack with tap? Add a simple "attack" — maybe swinging when pressing action near enemy. Keep it: enemies chase, damage over time; player health regen via food consumption.

Refuel: button uses wood/coal from inventory automatically when fuel low? Simpler: press "Fuel" button adds coal (25 fuel) or wood (15). Or auto: when boarding with resources, fuel converts. Let's have explicit Fuel button: consumes 1 coal -> +30 fuel; if no coal, 1 wood -> +20.

Win when reaching 2500m distance marker. Lose when player health 0 or... fuel out far from resources is recoverable (train just stopped, go gather). Death = game over with restart.

Rendering: canvas 2D, world coordinates: track at x=0; terrain generated deterministically by y (seeded chunks): trees, rocks, coal deposits, scrap, buildings/stations every 400m. Camera centered on player or train when aboard.

Train visual: top-down locomotive with coal car, maybe a wagon.

Enemies: zombies spawn near old stations; simple.

Controls: left half touch = joystick; right side buttons rendered as DOM (fixed positioned). Prevent scrolling: touch-action none, overflow hidden, 100dvh.

Also support keyboard/mouse for desktop testing (WASD).

World: y increases downward on screen but "forward" = decreasing y (north). Distance traveled = -trainY/10 (10px per meter). Track x = 0.

Camera: when aboard, cam centers on train (fixed x 0, y = train.y). When off, camera follows player. Camera x maybe follows player smoothly too but clamped so train visible? Simple: camera centers on player when off; on board, centers on train.

Generate props per chunk: trees (obstacle, give wood when chopped? simplify: wood piles), coal rocks, scrap metal, food (canned), grass tufts decorative, buildings. Each resource node has y, x offset, type, amount. Store in Map by chunk index for caching.

Enemies: spawn at stations (every 500m) in chunks near stations; simple chase AI within radius of spawn. Damage on contact 8/s.

Player: circle, speed 160 px/s, health 100. Attack: tap "Hit" button swings — damages enemies within 40px, cooldown 0.5s. Simplify: enemies die after 3 hits.

Collecting: walk over resource node; auto-collect with small delay/particles. Node depletes.

Boarding: when train stopped and player within 60px of train, show "Board" button; when aboard, "Get Off" button. Toggling stop: "Stop"/"Go" button always visible.

While aboard, player position = train position (drawn on train). Resources near track may be visible from train; you stop, get off, walk to them.

Distance HUD: meters traveled, goal 3000m. Win screen with stats.

## IRON HAUL — what you get

**The loop (Dead-Rails-inspired, top-down):**
- 🚂 Your train rolls north along a vertical track automatically, burning fuel as it goes
- **STOP** it (must be aboard to drive), **GET OFF**, and forage **coal / wood / canned food / scrap** scattered across procedurally generated wasteland
- Shovel coal (+40 ⛽) or wood (+24 ⛽) into the fire, then climb back aboard and keep rolling
- Goal: reach **Station Aurora at 3000 m** alive

**Threats & tension:**
- Zombies shamble around every depot (4 chunks) — they chase harder the deeper you go
- Your hammer swing (52px arc, 3 hits to kill) keeps them off while you loot
- Stand on the tracks while the train moves and it hurts you — but the train **run-overs zombies for scrap**
- Train runs out of fuel mid-wilderness? Walk back along the track (an arrow points the way) and refuel by hand

**Mobile-first, zero scrolling:**
- `position:fixed` + `touch-action:none` + `100dvh` — the page *cannot* scroll or zoom
- Left-thumb **dynamic joystick** (appears where you touch), context-sensitive buttons on the right: **STOP/GO · FUEL · EAT · big GET OFF / BOARD / HIT**
- Safe-area insets for notches, tap-highlight & double-tap-zoom suppressed
- Portrait-designed; also plays on desktop (WASD + Space/F/E/T)

**Verified via headless screenshots:** aboard-view (headlight, smoke, driver in cab), off-train looting with auto-pickup, zombie chase, win/death overlays, title card, and two phone sizes (360×740, 430×932) — all correct.

**Assumptions I made:** scrap is score/loot value (win-screen stat), the train only drives while you're aboard, food heals only when you're off the train, and the run is one long straight track with difficulty scaling by distance rather than branching rails. Debug hooks (`?shot=`, `&sim=`, `&probe=`) are left in — they're invisible during normal play and handy for future testing.

content.text:
The user wants three things:
1. Improve the train model visuals (better locomotive look)
2. Build more carts that the train drags — with a build/craft system
3. Walk around ON your train even while it's moving — and each cart type does different things and looks unique

Let me think about how to implement this well in the existing architecture.

## Design

### Cart system
Cart types (each unique look + function):
- **Coal tender** (starter, included): stores fuel capacity? Currently fuel is a single bar. Could give base fuel capacity.
- **Flatbed / Scraper** — collects scrap automatically when running over zombies/resources on track? Currently running over zombies gives scrap. Keep: kills zombies on track → scrap, look: flat wooden bed with stakes.
- **Boxcar** — storage + workshop: where you BUILD carts (build menu when standing in boxcar / at workshop). Actually make the **Caboose/Workshop**: allows building new carts while aboard (button appears when player is standing in workshop cart zone).
- **Plow / Cowcatcher cart in front?** — front-mounted plow clears obstacles/rock on track? There are no track obstacles yet. Could add: rocks/trees ON the track occasionally that damage the train unless plowed... That adds gameplay! Add "track debris" that appears on the track; hitting it without a plow damages train hull. With a plow cart in front, debris is cleared automatically (+scrap).
- **Bunker/Coal cart** — increases max fuel.
- **Medic/Bed cart** — regenerates HP slowly while player stands on it.
- **Armored turret cart?** — auto-shoots zombies nearby? That's fun but more work. Maybe simple: kills zombies within radius every 2s with a shot visual. Nice reward.
- **Fuel tank cart** — auto-converts wood→fuel slowly while moving (auto-feeder)! Actually simpler: holds fuel capacity +60 and shows liquid.
- **Greenhouse cart** — grows food over time (food ticks up slowly while moving), unique look with planters.

Keep the build list manageable: I'll implement 5 buildable carts + starting locomotive+tender:
1. **PLOW** (front) — clears track debris, prevents hull damage. Look: wedge, metal.
2. **BOXCAR** (workshop) — building happens here; look: big box with roof hatch.
3. **BUNKER** — +40 max fuel, look: coal heaped high with chute.
4. **GREENHOUSE** — +1 food per 20s while moving; look: glass roof, planters.
5. **TURRET** — auto-fires at zombies within 220px every 1.5s; look: rotating gun on platform.
6. **MEDIC/BUNK BEDS** — heal 2 HP/s while aboard standing on it; look: bunk + red cross.
7. **TANKER** — +fuel cap and auto refuel? redundant with bunker. Skip.

Maybe 5 buildables is plenty: PLOW, BOXCAR(workshop is required first?), BUNKER, GREENHOUSE, TURRET, MEDIC. Let me do: plow, workshop(boxcar), bunker, greenhouse, turret, medic — 6 types with costs in wood/coal/scrap/food.

Costs (wood W, coal C, scrap S):
- Workshop BOXCAR: 6W 4S (needed to build more)
- PLOW: 8W 6S
- BUNKER: 5W 2C 4S
- GREENHOUSE: 8W 2S 1 food seed?
- TURRET: 4W 2C 8S
- MEDIC: 6W 4S 2 food?

Building: press BUILD button while aboard (or while standing in workshop cart). New cart attaches at the rear (train grows). Train length affects handling? Keep simple: just longer.

### Walking on the train
Player position is currently world coords. The train is a vertical entity at x=0 with carts at y offsets. To walk on the train while it moves, the player's position when "on train deck" must be relative to the train (local coords), because carts move at train speed.

New model: player has a `deck` state:
- `deck === null`: off train entirely (world coords, walking on ground)
- `deck !== null`: player is ON a cart (local x within cart width, local y position along train), moves with the train.

Player aboard the train: starts in loco cab (driving). Walking: when player moves with joystick while deck != null, they move in local coords; if they walk off the edge of the train (beyond cart half-width ± a small margin, or beyond ends), they fall off → become off-train (world coords at that position). That's the "leave the cabin" — you can also just press GET OFF to hop off near the cab.

Collision on deck: carts block sideways (railings) so walking off the side only at gaps? Simpler: walking off side edge = fall off (intentional). Walking off front/back between carts: carts are connected — so the deck is continuous along the train (all carts flush). Front of locomotive: falling off front → hop off ahead (dangerous, train behind you). Rear of caboose: fall off back.

While on deck and train moving: fine, world coords track = train.y + local.

Zombie interactions while on deck? Zombies could climb aboard?? That's extra; maybe zombies can attack you on deck if adjacent (they're below). Keep: zombies can't reach you on deck (safe but you can't loot). But debris/plow still matters.

Player draw position: if deck != null, world pos = (localX + train.x=0, train.y + localY). Draw player standing on deck (above cart roof drawing? draw order: carts, then player on top). Player is on the ROOF? Top-down view — "walk around on your train" reads fine as walking along the deck/roof. Draw player on top of carts. 

Deck bounds: train structure: locomotive (front, y from t.y-150 to t.y-70), then carts stacked behind (each ~64px long), caboose at rear. Deck rect: x ∈ [-24, 24] (loco body ±24, carts ±22... use ±23), y ∈ [t.y-146, t.y-rearY+?]. Falling off: if player local |x| > 26 → fall to ground (world x = sign*(30+dist)). If player local y < -150 (front) or > rear+6 (back) → fall off that end.

Hmm, falling off the side while train is moving should be punishing: falling = get off at that spot; if train moving you drop beside it — no damage unless on tracks. Add small damage 5? No, keep no damage, it's a feature (jump off anywhere).

While on deck, joystick movement: local movement speed same. The world scroll continues (train moving), so the ground under player scrolls — cool effect automatically since draw is world-based and camera follows train when deck != null.

Camera: when deck != null, camera follows train (or player world pos which moves with train) — same thing. When off train, camera follows player.

Collecting resources while on deck: no (must be off). Fueling while in loco/anywhere on deck: FUEL button works when deck != null (you're on the train). Driving: STOP/GO works when deck != null and player is in the loco cab? Requiring the cab is more simulation-y: only the loco cab (localY < -70) can drive. Hmm, that could frustrate: you stop the train, walk back to greenhouse, harvest, walk back to cab to go. That's actually GOOD gameplay (dead rails-ish) but on mobile maybe annoying. Compromise: STOP works anywhere on deck (emergency brake), but GO requires being in the cab. Nice touch: toast "Walk to the cab to drive".

Building: BUILD button enabled when standing in workshop cart zone (localY within workshop cart range). Opens a small modal listing carts with costs; tap to build → attaches to rear. 

Food harvest: greenhouse — while player stands in greenhouse zone, tap EAT? Or automatic: greenhouse produces +1 food per 25s while moving, capped storage 3. Auto-produce, shown with plants growing on roof (3 stages). Simpler and readable.

Turret: auto-target nearest zombie within 230px of turret center, fires every 1.4s, bullet instant line + damage 1, muzzle flash. Look: rotating barrel.

Medic: while player's local position within medic cart and deck != null, +2 hp/s (only when train stopped? while moving too — fine).

Plow: train front gets plow; debris on track auto-cleared within plow zone → +1 scrap each, sparks. Without plow: debris hit → hull damage (train HP? new mechanic...). Hmm, hull damage needs train HP. Do I want train damage? It adds fail state: train breaks → stranded. Keep simple: hitting debris without plow: train jolts, player on deck takes 5 damage and gets knocked, debris remains? Actually simpler: debris always breaks when hit; without plow you lose 6 fuel (knocked off boiler) and screen shake; with plow you gain 1 scrap and no loss. Debris spawns on track occasionally (rocks/logs). This avoids adding train HP while making plow valuable.

Wait — but debris should be dodgeable? The train is on rails, can't dodge. It's just periodic events. Rate: every ~25s of movement, spawn debris ahead within next screen. Telegraph: warning "!" marker ahead + toast "Debris on the tracks!". Player can stop, walk, clear it manually? Clearing debris by hand: HIT it when off train near it (2 hits) → +2 wood (logs). Nice: another reason to stop.

Implement debris as props type 'debris' on track (x=0) generated in chunks (rare: chance per chunk ~35%? every 420px = 42m... at 10 m/s a debris every ~30-60s of travel). Spawn logic: in genChunk, if r() < 0.3 add debris at x=0, y within chunk, type 'rock' or 'log' (log gives wood when cleared by hand). Plow clears automatically when train passes (plow zone = front edge), giving scrap or wood.

Debris visual: pile of rocks or log across rails.

### Cart visual designs (each unique)
Train now: locomotive + tender (starter) + built carts appended rearward.

Draw each cart ~64px long, width 44px:
- **Tender (starter)**: dark steel, coal heap visible top with fuel-level-dependent fill, side ladder stripes.
- **Loco**: improved — boiler with rivets (dots), dome, chimney with smoke, cab with roof, cowcatcher front wedge if no plow, red nose band, gold trim, headlight.
- **Workshop boxcar**: rust-red box, roof hatch open with amber light glow, wrench sign on side, workbench edge visible? side planks.
- **Bunker**: black hopper with coal mound peaks, side chutes, yellow hazard stripes.
- **Greenhouse**: white frame, glass roof (translucent cyan panes with sheen), green planters inside visible through glass, growing plants scale with stored food.
- **Turret**: flat grey bed, sandbag ring, rotating barrel (angle = toward target or forward), ammo boxes.
- **Medic**: white cart with red cross on roof, stretcher rails, red/white stripe.
- **Plow**: mounted at front: steel wedge with bolts, brush guards (vertical bars), headlight mounted on it? The loco keeps its headlight. Plow wedge V shape.

Also: carts connected with couplers (dark links, gap 6px).

### Deck walking details
Local coordinate system: define cart layout array computed from S.train.carts (list of type strings, first is loco implicit, then tender + built ones... Actually loco is always first; tender always second (starter). Built carts appended after. Rear-most cart acts as caboose (no separate caboose; the last cart gets a red rear lamp).

Layout computation: 
```
const CART_LEN = 66, GAP = 8;
segments: loco: from front tip y=0 (local, 0 = front bumper) extending back 150? Let me define local y: 0 at loco front, increasing rearward. Cart i spans [locoLen + i*(CART_LEN+GAP), ... + CART_LEN]. World y of local position: worldY = train.y - localY? If local 0 = front and front is the northernmost point: world front = train.y - 150 (since train.y is our reference... currently train.y was cab center). Let me redefine: train.y = world y of the FRONT bumper. Loco spans worldY [t.y, t.y+150]. Cart i spans [t.y + frontOffset_i, ...+CART_LEN]. Deck position local: ly measured from front bumper rearward.
```

Cab zone: ly ∈ [8, 140]?? Loco: front bumper at ly=0, boiler from ly=0..100, cab ly=100..150. Drive zone: ly ∈ [100,150]. Walk on: hop-off default position was beside cab. GET OFF button: hop off the side at player's current deck position (world pos = current). So GET OFF = fall off side at current spot (nice, replaces "hop off").

BOARD: when off train near any part of the train (dist to nearest cart segment < 50?) and train stopped → climb onto deck at nearest point (ly = that point's local ly, lx = side edge). While moving: allow boarding?? Real trains — you can't. Require stopped. But the player might want to re-board while it moves... no, keep stopped requirement (else trivializes). On deck you're safe from zombies (they can't climb). Acceptable — your mobile fortress. The danger is fuel + debris + getting off.

Hmm, but then late game with turret + medic you're unkillable... fine, it's a cozy builder-runner. The challenge: fuel economy and detours.

### Build UI
When standing in workshop zone (or any deck position? no — workshop only), show BUILD button (replaces/ACT?). Buttons layout: we have TRAIN, FUEL, ACT, EAT. Add BUILD. Context ACT already used for GET OFF/HIT. I'll add a 5th button BUILD (🔧) that's grayed unless in workshop zone. FUEL_MAX currently 100. Bunker cart: +40 each. FUEL_MAX = 100 + 40*bunkerCount. uiSync uses FUEL_MAX — make it a function trainFuelMax(). Fuel bar max adjusts; when building bunker, fuel stays same value.

State: S.train.gGrow (timer), S.train.gStore (0..3). While moving (or stopped? photosynthesis needs sun... while moving, why? make it always tick but slower stopped? Keep: while moving +1 per 18s up to 3; plants on roof show growth = store/3). When player stands in greenhouse zone → harvest: store → food (button: use ACT? ACT is GET OFF...). Every 1.4s while zombies exist within 240px of turret world center: fire: damage 1 to nearest, draw tracer line for 0.1s (store beam in S.beams with ttl), muzzle puff. Sound? none.

### Train length & turning? 
No turning. Train length grows; camera aboard: center on train center of mass? Camera focus: currently t.y (front). With longer train, better to focus on player when on deck (player world pos) — yes! When deck != null, camera follows player world pos (which rides with train) — smooth and always shows the player. When in cab driving, camera at cab. That's better than focusing front bumper. Define segments builder:

```js
const LOCO_LEN = 150, CART_LEN = 62, COUP = 10, TENDER0 = 160;
function segs(){
  const out = [{ type:'loco', y0: 0, y1: LOCO_LEN }];
  out.push({ type:'tender', y0: TENDER0, y1: TENDER0 + CART_LEN });
  let off = TENDER0 + CART_LEN + COUP;
  for (const c of S.train.carts){ out.push({ ...c, y0: off, y1: off + CART_LEN }); off += CART_LEN + COUP; }
  return out; // worldY = t.y + y0..y1
}
function trainLen(){ return TENDER0 + CART_LEN + (CART_LEN+COUP) * S.train.carts.length; }
function zoneAt(ly){
  const t = S.train;
  if (ly < LOCO_LEN) return { type:'loco', y0:0, y1:LOCO_LEN };
  if (ly < TENDER0) return null;
  if (ly < TENDER0 + CART_LEN) return { type:'tender', ... };
  let off = TENDER0 + CART_LEN + COUP;
  for (const c of t.carts){ if (ly < off + CART_LEN) return {...c, y0:off, y1:off+CART_LEN}; off += CART_LEN+COUP; }
  return null;
}
```

function trainNear(p, maxD){

}

## What changed

### 🚂 Train visual overhaul
The locomotive is now properly detailed: red buffer beam, riveted boiler with gold bands, steam dome, sandbox, chimney, cab with lit skylights and roof overhang, side running boards, visible wheels, plus a **rear lamp** on the last car and a headlight beam when rolling.

### 🔧 Cart building (via a new Workshop car)
Stand inside the **Workshop car** → BUILD opens a crafting panel with live cost chips (red when short) — new cars bolt onto the rear of the consist, and the train visibly grows:

| Car | Cost | What it does / looks like |
|---|---|---|
| **Workshop** | 6🪵 4⚙️ | Opens the build menu — rust-red planked boxcar, glowing open roof hatch, wrench plate |
| **Cow Plow** | 8🪵 6⚙️ | Steel wedge ahead of the loco — smashes track debris for scrap (no plow = 💥 thud, −6 fuel + screen shake) |
| **Coal Bunker** | 5🪵 2⚫ 4⚙️ | **+40 max fuel** — black hopper, hazard stripes, fuel gauge drawn as the coal heap height |
| **Greenhouse** | 8🪵 2⚙️ 1🥫 | Grows food **while rolling** (3 stages, plants visibly grow) — glass roof, planters, walk in to auto-harvest |
| **Turret** | 4🪵 2⚫ 8⚙️ | Auto-fires at infected near the train — sandbag ring, barrel that **rotates to track targets**, tracer beams |
| **Infirmary** | 6🪵 4⚙️ 2🥫 | Heals you while you stand on it — white car with big red cross |

### 🚶 Walk your train — even while it's moving
- The player now lives in the train's **local coordinate space** while aboard: walk the whole deck with the joystick as the ground scrolls past, drive from the **cab zone** (STOP works anywhere, GO needs the cab — button hints "CAB"), then **jump off any side, front or rear** at speed
- Cart zones drive interactions: bunker fueling anywhere on deck, workshop building, greenhouse harvesting, infirmary healing
- Couplers connect cars; the consist drags you along seamlessly

### New hazard: track debris
Logs and rock piles now spawn on the rails with a pulsing **"!"** warning + toast ahead of impact — plow through, brake and clear them by hand (2 hits → wood/coal/scrap), or eat a fuel penalty.

Balance tweak: zombie contact damage flash softened; boarding still requires a stopped train. Debug hooks extended (`?shot=deck|build|plow|zom2`) — invisible in normal play.

Now let's think about the **fuel display** and **low fuel warning**. At start, 55 fuel, moving; the low fuel warning triggers at <20 around 23s/240m. The HUD number counts down. Good.

**Out of fuel**: The train stops when fuel hits 0; the player can refuel. But `doFuel` requires aboard; if out of fuel, the player is likely aboard; fine. If the player is off, they can board a stopped train. Good.

**Health regen**: only medic. Food heals off-train. Good.

**No stamina**. Fine.

One more possible issue: **the player can collect resources while standing on the moving train?** `nearestRes` is only called in the off-train branch. Good.

**When the player gets off a moving train, then the train moves away; the camera follows the player; the HUD offscreen indicator shows the train's direction and distance.** Verified in the draw code. Good.

Let me test the offscreen indicator by moving the player far from the train and screenshotting. The `?shot=off` screenshot showed the train at the bottom edge but not the indicator because the train was within 30px of the screen. Let's set a farther position. Not essential, but check the code:
```
const sy = S.train.y + oy;
if (sy < -30 || sy > H+30) { ax=W/2; ay=clamp(sy,40,H-90); dirn = sy<0?-1:1; arrow; text '🚂 N m' }
```
If the train is above (sy<0), the arrow is at y=40 and points up. If below, at H-90, points down. Good. The distance is `Math.abs(S.train.y - S.player.y)/PPM`, which is the distance to the train's **front**, not the nearest car. If the player is at the rear, the distance shown is to the front (may be 30m more). Minor. Could use the nearest segment, but fine.

**The offscreen indicator only when off train.** Good.

**On-deck camera**: `S.focusF` = .6, so the player is at 60% height; looking ahead. Good.

**Player speed** 170 vs train 105; can walk from cab to rear while moving in (trainLen 300px / 170 = 1.8s) but the camera follows. Good.

**Train length with 6 carts**: 160+62+10*? `trainLen=160+62+(62+10)*6=654` px = 65m. The camera view in portrait 844 shows ~84m vertical, so most of the train. Fine.

**Building a cart while standing in the workshop and the train is moving**: pause; add at rear; resume. The player is in the workshop, which remains; the new car extends behind. Good.

**If the workshop is destroyed?** No destruction.

**Mobile `touch-action`**: The canvas is fixed; buttons use touch-action manipulation. Good.

near the gesture handlers.

Also `window.addEventListener('keydown', ...)` currently doesn't prevent default for arrows; add:

if (['ArrowUp','ArrowDown','ArrowLeft','ArrowRight'].includes(e.key)) e.preventDefault();

Edited index.html (1 replacement)

Now, a **quality of life** feature: when interacting with the BUILD button off the workshop, the toast says "Walk into the workshop car to build". But the button is dim and intercepting taps? A dim button still calls act and gives the toast. Good.

When the BUILD button is off because the player is off-train, tapping it gives "Climb aboard to build". Good.

When the player is aboard without a workshop, the BUILD button is active; tapping opens the modal. Good.

When the player is in the workshop with no materials, all ADD buttons dim. Tapping a dim ADD calls buildCart → "Not enough materials". Good.

**One bug**: In the build modal, the dim ADD buttons are still clickable and the cost rows show red; okay.

**One bug**: After building a cart, `renderBuildList` is called but `uiSync` isn't, so the HUD chips are stale while paused. The build modal's cost rows refresh from S.inv, so the player sees correct affordability. On closing, uiSync refreshes within .12s. Fine. But if the player buys a bunker, the max fuel increases and the HUD fuel bar isn't updated until close. Fine.

**One bug**: Building a bunker while paused increases fuelMax but not fuel; when closing, the bar drops. Fine.

**One bug**: The first workshop purchase auto-closes the modal and unpauses, but the build button's off state won't update until uiSync. Since the train resumes, uiSync runs. Fine.

**One bug**: The first workshop purchase calls `puff(0, S.train.y + trainLen() - 40, ...)` **after** pushing the workshop, so trainLen includes the new car; the puff is at its rear. Good.

**One bug**: `buildCart` calls `closeBuild()` for the first workshop, then the caller may continue? It returns immediately after closeBuild. Good.

Now, **the user's original issue** was BUILD always saying stand in workshop. We fixed by allowing the first workshop. But what if the user's expectation is that the BUILD button should work **everywhere**? The design still requires standing in the workshop after the first build. The summary says "Workshop building must be usable from an accessible location on the train." The accessible location is the workshop car. We've added a marker and auto-close. Good.

Would it be better to make the BUILD button open the catalogue anywhere aboard, and require the workshop only for *building*? The user complained the condition never works; our fix ensures it does. Fine.

Let's test **walking into the workshop** visually with the marker and the gold outline from a real start, not state injection. Our playtest did that. Good.

One more issue: **The workshop zone detection after building the first workshop**. The player is at the cab and the workshop is at the rear. If they hold ArrowDown, they pass the tender and enter the workshop. `inZone('workshop')` uses `ly >= off && ly < off+CART_LEN`, off=232. The player moving at 170px/s crosses in ~0.08s; fine.

**On-deck collision**: The player can walk over the gap; no collision. Fine.

**The `blocked` function** prevents the off-train player from crossing the train; to board, they stand near. Fine.

**The off-train boarding radius**: `trainNear(60)` uses the lateral clamp; if the player is within 60px of the train side and any y within the train, can board. That's generous. When moving, they can jump on. Good.

**When off train and standing at x=0 (on the tracks) with the train stopped**, `trainNear(60)` returns 0 (since p.x clamp = 0) and canBoard true; pressing BOARD teleports to the train at ly = clamp(trainNear - t.y) = clamp(p.y - t.y). If the player is on the track **inside the train's footprint** (blocked prevents walking into it, but they could be on the track ahead/behind), boarding works. Fine.

Now, let's decide on adding **sound**. I'll skip, but maybe add a subtle **screen shake** on hits (already), **puffs** (already), **floating texts** (already). The game feels alive without sound.

**Performance on mobile**: The draw loop renders all props in view + train + particles. It should be 60fps. The chunk generation is cached. Fine.

**Memory**: particles/texts capped naturally by life. Zombies capped at 42 on spawn; also cleaned if >1900 from camera. Fine.

**One potential crash**: `nearestRes()` returns a prop; `collect(p)` for a `tree` adds wood; for a `rock`, `collect` does nothing (names has no rock, type not tree). But `nearestRes` includes any prop with `amt` and not taken, including `rock`? `rock` props are pushed with `amt: 1 + (r()*3|0)`! Yes, in `genChunk`, all random props, including `rock` and `grass`, get `amt`. `nearestRes`:
```
for (const p of propsInView(...)) {
  if (!p.amt || p.amt<=0 || p.taken) continue;
  const d=...
  if (d<30) return p;
}
```
It can return a **rock** or **grass** prop. `collect(p)`:
- names has coal/wood/scrap/food → add
- tree → wood
- else nothing (rock/grass)
So walking near a rock or grass **silently marks it `taken`**, making it disappear, with no reward! This is a **bug**: grass tufts and rocks can be "collected" and vanish, and more importantly, a rock near you could be picked up (taken=true) without yielding anything; the player might wonder why rocks disappear. Also, `nearestRes` prioritizes the nearest prop regardless of type; a grass tuft near a coal node could be collected instead, and since it doesn't award anything, the player misses the coal. Actually `collect` marks the grass taken, then next frame `nearestRes` finds the coal and collects it. But the grass disappearing is odd.

Fix: restrict `nearestRes` to collectible types: `['coal','wood','scrap','food','tree']`. That also prevents rocks/grass from being picked up. Use a constant `RES_TYPES` or inline check. This is a real bug worth fixing for "finish".

Also, **trees** award `amt+1` wood; a tree has a collision radius 31 and `blocked` prevents the player from getting within 31px, while `nearestRes` requires distance <30. So you can never collect a tree! The collision radius is 31, and the collection radius is 30, plus the player is a point — `blocked` prevents moving to a point within 31 of the tree center. You could stand at 31.1, not <30. So trees are **uncollectible**. The tree is a resource that should give wood. Let's examine:
```
blocked: if (p.type==='tree' && !p.taken && Math.hypot(x-p.x,y-p.y) < 31) return true;
nearestRes: bd=30; if (d<bd)...
```
The player's position is checked against the tree center; to collect, they need d<30, but blocked stops them at 31. They can never get d<30. **Trees are purely decorative obstacles**, despite having `amt` and the collect logic. The random `tree` roll is 30% of nodes; if the player can't collect them, 30% of resource nodes are useless. Hmm! But wait, the player can approach the tree diagonally; `blocked(nx, ny)` returns true if the **new position** is within 31 of a tree. It allows moving from a position at d=31.2 to a position at d=30.9? The check is on the new position; if d<31, blocked. So the minimum distance is >=31. Collection is <30. Impossible. Unless the player's collection check uses `propsInView(S.player.y, 200)` around p.y; still d>=31.

This is a **major bug**: trees are never collectible, and 30% of the resource rolls are trees. The player can still gather wood from the `wood` nodes (14%), but the tree art suggests choppable. The "HIT" action can hit debris only, not trees. The original intent may be that trees are obstacles, not resources. But `collect` handles 'tree' with +wood, and `nearestRes` includes them, so clearly intended to be collectible. Maybe the tree's collision radius should be smaller (e.g., 18) or the collection radius bigger (e.g., 38). Let's make trees collectible by raising the pickup radius for trees to 38 while keeping the collision at 31. Simplest: in `nearestRes`, use `const bd = 30` but for tree use 38? The function returns the nearest; implement:
```
const reach = p.type==='tree' ? 40 : 30;
if (d < reach)...
```
But the loop currently uses a single `bd` initialized 30 and updates `bd=d`. Change to:
```
let best=null,bd=30;
for (...) {
  ...
  const reach = p.type==='tree'?40:30;
  if (d < reach && d < bd) { bd=d; best=p; }
}
```
This lets the player collect a tree from 39px away, outside the 31 collision. Note the player may be near multiple resources; the nearest wins. Trees at 31-40 can be collected. Good.

Also, `collect` for trees adds wood +1 and `p.amt+1`. Good.

**Rocks** are obstacles with no purpose; leaving them uncollectible is fine. **Grass** decorative. Restrict nearestRes to collectible types so they don't vanish.

**Debris** is also a prop with `amt` but `nearestRes` currently includes it! `propsInView` includes debris with `amt` (1-3) and `taken` false. Walking within 30 of debris would call `collect`, which does nothing and marks it taken! That means **debris on the tracks is silently removed when the player walks near it**, and the HIT action can't be used because it's taken. Even worse: debris is drawn on the rails; an off-train player walking near it might accidentally collect it without reward. The HIT action checks `d.type !== 'debris' || d.taken` and would skip. So this is a real bug. Restricting nearestRes to resource types fixes it.

Also, `depot` has no `amt`; fine.
`sign`/`finish` no amt.
`zs` prop has no amt? `spawnZs` gets a prop with n; no amt. Fine.
`patch` no amt.
`debris` has amt → currently collectible. Fix.

So **critical fixes**:
```
const RES_PICK = {coal:1, wood:1, scrap:1, food:1, tree:1};
function nearestRes(){
  let best=null,bd=30;
  for (const p of propsInView(S.player.y, 200)){
    if (!RES_PICK[p.type] || !p.amt || p.amt<=0 || p.taken) continue;
    const d = ...
    const reach = p.type==='tree' ? 40 : 30;
    if (d < reach && d < bd){ bd=d; best=p; }
  }
  return best;
}
```
Wait, `bd` initialized 30; for a tree at d=35, `d<reach` true but `d<bd` (35<30) false → not collected. Need to initialize `bd = 40` or track best distance separately. Use:
```
let best=null, bd=1e9;
...
const reach = p.type==='tree'?40:30;
if (d < reach && d < bd) { bd=d; best=p; }
```
Then a tree at 35 is selected if no closer resource. But if a coal node is at 29 and a tree at 35, `bd` becomes 29 and the tree isn't selected; the coal is collected first. Good. If the tree is at 35 and no other resource, selected. Fine. `bd` starting at 1e9 but `reach` limits.

But then **a tree at 31** (the closest possible) is selected. Good.

Also, with the tree collision at 31, can the player get within 40? Yes. Collecting marks it taken; the next `blocked` ignores taken trees (`p.type==='tree' && !p.taken`), so the player can walk through where it was. Good.

Now, the **`blocked` function for rocks** always blocks, even if `p.taken` (rocks can't be taken now). Fine.

The **`collect` for tree** award `p.amt+1`; with amt 1-3 → 2-4 wood per tree. Good.

This is a significant game-balance fix. Let's implement.

Also, check **coal/wood/scrap/food pickup radius** 30 vs their collision? They have no collision, so fine.

**Debris hand-hitting**: `doAct` off-train when not near a resource hits debris within 52. Good, now debris won't be accidentally collected.

**Debris `propsInView`** includes `taken` false. The train collision independently handles debris. Good.

**Trees and the train**: `blocked` only for off-train; the train passes through trees? Trees are off the track (|x|>75), so fine.

Let's implement `nearestRes`.

Now test resource collection incl. tree and debris not auto-collected. Let's write a targeted test:
- Place a tree prop near the player, set player just outside 31 but inside 42, call nearestRes/collect, verify wood increases and tree taken.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first top-down train survival game inspired by Roblox’s Dead Rails, and make cart building accessible and functional.

## Requirements
- Train moves forward; player can stop, disembark to gather resources, reboard, and continue.
- Mobile-first fixed layout with no page scrolling; desktop controls are also available.
- Player can walk around the train while it is moving; carts have unique looks and functions.
- Workshop building must be usable from an accessible location on the train.

## Decisions
- Single-file game named **IRON HAUL**, with a straight procedural route and 3000 m destination.
- First workshop can be built while aboard; further carts require standing inside a workshop car.

## Work State

### Completed
- `index.html` contains the game, HUD, resource gathering/fueling, combat, zombies, win/death states, and mobile-friendly fixed layout.
- Train and cart visuals, walking on the moving consist, cart catalogue, and distinct cart designs and effects are implemented.
- Fixed workshop access flow: BUILD permits constructing the first workshop while aboard, then requires the player to stand inside a workshop for subsequent builds.
- Updated intro text to explain the workshop-building flow.
- Embedded JavaScript syntax validated with Node.

### Active
- (none)

- (none)

1. (none)

- `index.html`: Complete single-file game implementation, including workshop access and cart building.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first top-down train survival game inspired by Roblox’s Dead Rails, with accessible, functional cart building.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first train survival game inspired by Roblox’s Dead Rails, with accessible cart building and a five-biome journey to 5000 m.
- Improve the appearance of the player, enemies, and houses seen along the route.

## Requirements
- Train moves forward; player can stop, disembark to gather resources, reboard, and continue.
- Fixed, mobile-first layout without page scrolling; desktop controls are also available.
- Player can walk around the moving train; carts have distinct looks and functions.
- Workshop building must be accessible and functional from the train.
- The first workshop can be built while aboard; further carts require standing inside a workshop car.
- Five biomes span 0–5000 m, with 150 m blended transitions.

## Decisions
- Single-file game named **IRON HAUL**, with a straight procedural route.
- The 5000 m destination is Station Aurora; omit the 5000 m sign to avoid overlap with the finish line.

## Work State

### Completed
- `index.html` implements the game, including HUD, resource gathering and fueling, combat, zombies, win/death states, and a mobile-friendly fixed layout.
- Train movement, walking around the consist, cart catalogue, unique cart designs/effects, and workshop access/building flow are implemented.
- Five biomes are implemented with terrain, track colors, vegetation, landmarks, atmospheric effects, HUD, and transition banners.
- JavaScript syntax, browser gameplay regressions, full-route simulation, and mobile controls passed without browser errors.

### Active
- Improve the player and enemy visuals and the houses seen along the route.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and redesign the player, zombie, and depot/house artwork in `index.html`.
2. Run syntax and browser gameplay checks after the visual changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete single-file game; contains `drawPlayer`, zombie rendering and update logic, and depot drawing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is untracked in git.
- Recent inspection located `drawPlayer` near line 1255, zombie logic near line 461, and depot drawing near line 1111; no visual changes have been made yet.
